text:
Sarah (support): Heads-up: ACME webhook started failing JSON parsing after our model swap to v7c ~09:07 UTC. They say payload is valid but their consumer rejects it. Ticket SUP-9832. Attaching repro from their side and our logs below.

Mike (eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact request/response? streaming or non-streaming?

Sarah (support): Streaming. Their receiver gets a JSON parse error at the start of chunk 2. Our gateway logs show these bytes before chunk 2: 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF. Looks like a UTF-8 BOM sneaked in. Repro steps: 1) call /v1/chat with model=v7c structured_output=true 2) stream response to client 3) client fails on parse when concatenating chunks.

Sarah (support): Repro snippet (sanitized):
```
> client -> POST /v1/chat (stream: true)
> payload: {"prompt":"...","json_schema":{...}}

< stream chunk 1: "{\"order_id\": 123, \"items\": ["
< stream chunk 2: "\xef\xbb\xbf\"{\"id\": 1}\", \"...\" ] }"
```

Carla (oncall): Hmm can the model be emitting a U+FEFF or zero-width no-break space? I've seen tokeniser effects where certain generated tokens are represented as BOM-like bytes when encoding step flips.

Dave (eng-ml): We've got one hit earlier with a quantized LLM variant that prepended a BOM when generating `"` after a newline in streaming mode. Might be a kernel/encoder edge-case during chunk boundary characterization after the recent tokenizer tweak.

Leo (infra): deploy-bot shows model promotion at 3168001100 -> v7c canary -> flip at 3168001200 to stable for region us-west-2. That matches customer failure time.

deploy-bot: model-service: promoted model v7c to stable (canary 3168001100) by @release.

Sarah (support): Customer workaround: they switched to non-streaming and succeeded. But they need streaming. Asking for ETA on fix + if we should revert for customers with streaming enabled.

Mike (eng-runtime): Can you share the exact raw bytes from our edge logs (hex) and the model stdout? Also did we do any utf-8 re-encoding at the edge layer?

Sarah (support): Pasted hex from edge: 
```
... 7b 22 6f 72 64 65 72 5f 69 64 22 3a 20 31 32 33 2c 20 22 69 74 65 6d 73 22 3a 20 5b 0a  ef bb bf 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 20 31 7d 2c 20 ...
```

Mike (eng-runtime): OK. That is a real BOM byte sequence (EF BB BF) inserted right before a `{` at a chunk boundary. Two hypotheses: 1) model generated a U+FEFF char; 2) serialization path encoded a zero-width marker when reconstructing tokens for the second chunk. I'll try to reproduce locally with streaming harness.

Dave (eng-ml): I'll run the model locally with same tokenization and streaming encoder flags. If it's model output, we need a quick token-filtering fix (drop U+FEFF) in the streaming serializer as a short-term patch.

Irene (support): Customer wants a hotfix or an option we can toggle per-project. Any chance of providing `strip_bom=true` or `sanitize_stream=true` flag in the API so existing clients don't break?

Mike (eng-runtime): We can add a per-tenant sanitization middleware very quickly (10-20m) to strip leading U+FEFF or other zero-width chars when chunk starts with those bytes. Not ideal long-term but quick. Will coordinate with infra for rollout.

Leo (infra): Need a canary for the middleware in us-west-2 only. I can push a traffic-split with middleware enabled for customer org ACME.

Carla (oncall): @eng-runtime please also check if this interacts with gzip/chunked transfer encoding or content-length framing. I've seen BOMs introduced accidentally when a binary safe path flips.

Mike (eng-runtime): Noted. Repro plan: 1) run streaming harness against v7c with same prompt and schema 2) capture raw bytes 3) if BOM appears, add sanitizer in runtime and run canary. I'll post results here.

support-bot: Created incident/inc-2026-0042 for SUP-9832 and linked customer account ACME.

Sarah (support): Customer update: they'll accept a tenant-scoped sanitization for now. They ask whether we'll roll back v7c for streaming customers.

Dave (eng-ml): If model is root cause, we should file a model-onboarding bug with model team and add unit in model-wrapper to drop U+FEFF token from first byte of chunk.

Mike (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation plan: tenant-scoped sanitizer can go live in 30-45m, canary to ACME only. Longer term: identify whether the tokenizer or postprocessor inserted the char. If it's tokenizer, we need a model patch.

Carla (oncall): Assigning follow-ups: @Mike (eng-runtime) implement sanitizer, @Dave (eng-ml) reproduce + open model bug, @Leo (infra) canary rollout, @Irene keep customer updated with timeline.

Sarah (support): Thanks. I'll send customer a targeted invite for canary and update SUP-9832.

Mike (eng-runtime): Update — reproduced locally. BOM shows up when chunk boundary splits between a multi-byte sequence produced by postprocess. Pushing tenant middleware now to staging.

Leo (infra): Middleware staged. Requesting approval for canary to ACME in us-west-2.

Carla (oncall): Approved. @Leo proceed.

Leo (infra): Canary applied to ACME. Monitoring logs for stripped bytes and any latency impact.

Sarah (support): Customer confirmed they resumed streaming successfully after canary. They saw zero parse errors in 20 tests.

Mike (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: 1) add unit tests for chunk-boundary sanitization 2) model team to check tokenizer output for U+FEFF 3) consider rejecting model variants that emit non-printable markers in structured output mode.

Dave (eng-ml): Filed model bug: MODEL-1542 (tokenizer emits U+FEFF at certain offsets).

Carla (oncall): Closing loop: no rollback needed; tenant-level sanitizer applied until model patch lands. Logging will flag any future similar insertions.

Sarah (support): Closing SUP-9832 once we get final note from model team. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
